problem: VLN benchmarks evaluate each instruction independently in unseen environments with frozen parameters, ignoring that real robots operate in persistent scenes with consistent layouts and user speaking styles. Existing datasets also have too few evaluation buildings/instructions per scene, and no OOD data, to study scene adaptation.
motivation: Household or building robots see the same environment and the same instructors over time, so they should improve by adapting. This needs a benchmark with many instructions per scene, diverse building types (ID and OOD) and diverse speaking styles, plus a study of which adaptation mechanisms actually work.
key_idea: Define GSA-VLN, a single-scene lifelong adaptation task with the new GSA-R2R dataset, and propose GR-DUET, which keeps a persistent global topological graph across episodes and is trained with environment-specific graph buffers to match inference.
insight: Unsupervised optimization-based adaptation (TENT, SAR, MLM, MRC) gives no gain or hurts because entropy is unreliable in sequential decision-making, while explicit graph memory helps a lot. Naive history-embedding memory (TourHAMT, OVER-NAV) collapses, because long histories cause distribution shift. Ablation: pretraining on GT graphs plus PREVALENT augmentation are only effective together (Test-R-Basic SR 69.3 vs 59.9 / 54.0 alone), and buffer-style graph simulation beats random proportion of GT graph.
method: GSA-VLN task: agent has an environment-specific memory bank (instructions, observations, actions, paths) accessible as long-term history and usable for unsupervised parameter updates without feedback.

GSA-R2R environments: 150 buildings (75 residential as ID, 75 non-residential as OOD; HM3D + MP3D) selected via GPT-4 building-type classification, manual verification, and K-Means on layout metadata; 600 paths per scene.

Three-stage instruction orchestration: EnvDrop speaker generates instructions; failed ones (via a DUET-based feasibility check) are refined by GPT-4o with path visualizations and CoT to give Basic; GPT-4o rephrases into Scene (building-role style) and User (5 TV characters incl. child, RoleLLM-style) styles.
GR-DUET global graph: instead of a per-episode graph, keeps a single topological graph of all visited nodes (positions + observations) across episodes, resetting visited flags each episode.
Environment-specific training: pretrain DUET with the full GT topological map; fine-tune with a per-environment graph that grows over episodes and is re-initialized after alpha=50 episodes.
Augmentation: add PREVALENT data to increase graph coverage and path diversity in fine-tuning.
Baselines benchmarked: TENT, SAR, back-translation, MLM, MRC, TourHAMT, OVER-NAV.

setting.backbone: DUET (dual-scale graph transformer) with CLIP ViT-B/16 features, trained (GR-DUET)
setting.training_data: R2R train plus PREVALENT augmentation; pretraining with GT topological graphs; evaluation-time adaptation is only graph memory (no parameter update)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with discrete navigation graph
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (global action over topological map nodes)
setting.privileged: none (graph is built online from the agent's own previous episodes)

numbers.extra: PREVALENT augmentation, mean of 3 runs over random instruction orders
one environment per instruction type, for LLM comparison
numbers.evidence: Comparison of LLM-based methods and GR-DUET on GSA-R2R table, Test-N-Basic

numbers_note: GSA-R2R is a new benchmark not in the canonical list. Table 4 (User) reports only some characters and other characters (Keith 66.7/62.0, Moira 60.9/56.2, Rachel 67.1/62.2) are omitted. The abstract states an 8% SR gain over vanilla DUET.
results: GR-DUET achieves SOTA across all GSA-R2R splits, e.g. Test-R-Basic SR 69.3 vs DUET 57.7 (+11.6) and Test-N-Basic SR 56.6 vs 48.1 (+8.5), Test-N-Scene 48.1 vs 39.6. Back-translation is the strongest optimization baseline (61.3 SR on R-Basic), while TENT/SAR are below vanilla DUET and TourHAMT/OVER-NAV collapse to 10-22 SR. GR-DUET also beats LLM-based MapGPT and NavCoT on the sampled environments.
limitations: Basic instruction refinement by GPT-4o still contains errors because VLMs struggle with spatial relations between panoramas; only 5 User characters.
GR-DUET adapts only visually via graph memory, with no language-style-specific mechanism; adaptation is weak in multi-floor buildings with dissimilar layouts.
Covers only step-by-step instructions (not object-goal or dialog), and evaluated only in simulation.
